canonicalPages.title: Open urban heat planning
canonicalPages.description: An open, public-interest platform for understanding urban heat, cooling access, and transparent mitigation scenarios.

canonicalPages.title: Cities and heat evidence
canonicalPages.description: Explore city heat evidence, data readiness, and transparent public-interest urban heat workflows.
canonicalPages.summary: Boston is the bundled study city. Other city options help frame onboarding questions and need their own local sources before they can support place-specific conclusions.

canonicalPages.title: Boston urban heat study
canonicalPages.description: Inspect Boston urban heat and cooling-access evidence with source context, caveats, and transparent planning tools.
canonicalPages.summary: The Boston study connects a documented boundary and local overlays to an inspectable map. Check each layer's source, coverage, and limitations before drawing conclusions about a neighborhood.

canonicalPages.title: Urban heat mitigation scenarios
canonicalPages.description: Explore transparent, cost-aware urban heat mitigation scenarios and their stated assumptions.
canonicalPages.summary: Compare intervention mixes and budgets with the assumptions beside the results. Scenario outputs are exploratory benchmarks, not validated predictions of local temperature or health outcomes.

canonicalPages.title: Urban heat learning paths
canonicalPages.description: Choose an accessible learning and planning path for understanding local heat, evidence, and action.
canonicalPages.summary: Start with a path matched to your question, then move into city evidence, scenarios, or methods. Each path keeps the distinction between observations, model outputs, and decisions visible.

canonicalPages.title: Urban heat data exports
canonicalPages.description: Access transparent urban heat planning exports and supporting evidence artifacts.
canonicalPages.summary: Find available output artifacts and inspect their provenance before reuse. The source record and stated limits matter as much as the exported file.

canonicalPages.title: Urban heat run history
canonicalPages.description: Review transparent urban heat workflow executions, artifacts, and logs.
canonicalPages.summary: Inspect available runs and their outputs to understand what inputs and processing produced an analysis. A run record supports reproducibility; it does not establish field validity on its own.

canonicalPages.title: Urban heat robustness lab
canonicalPages.description: Explore a transparent synthetic demonstration of spectral, reliability, and percolation reasoning for urban heat planning.
canonicalPages.summary: Use a synthetic example to inspect graph connectivity, reliability, and percolation measures. These graph properties are precise for their stated inputs and are not measured city outcomes.

canonicalPages.title: Interactive urban heat mitigation lab
canonicalPages.description: Explore cooling interventions with a bounded browser priority field and separate graph metrics. Outputs are not local temperature forecasts.
canonicalPages.summary: Try placement ideas in a bounded browser priority field and inspect graph changes separately. The lab is a way to ask better questions about possible cooling actions, not a site-specific engineering forecast.

canonicalPages.title: Address-level cooling action plan
canonicalPages.description: Build a privacy-first, evidence-bounded starting plan for heat safety, local observation, and collective cooling action.
canonicalPages.summary: Turn an address-level question into a starting checklist for local observation and collective action. Verify conditions on the ground and follow current public-health guidance for immediate heat-safety decisions.

canonicalPages.title: Urban heat solution suite and GIS tools
canonicalPages.description: Interactive GIS API playgrounds, OSM infrastructure query builders, sensor validation benches, and federal climate grant generators.
canonicalPages.summary: Explore GIS and infrastructure queries, sensor checks, and planning aids. These tools help assemble an auditable question; review source quality and local requirements before using their output in a proposal.

canonicalPages.title: Collaborate on urban heat action
canonicalPages.description: A clear path for communities, mentors, public partners, and researchers to contribute to accountable urban heat work.
canonicalPages.summary: Bring a bounded place-based question, relevant evidence, or lived context. Community members, public partners, mentors, and researchers can help challenge assumptions and shape a responsible next step.
